1.
We have elaborately heard the learned advocates for either of the parties.
2. In order to examine as to what relief the writ petitioner is entitled to, we require a comprehensive report to be filed by the 3 rd respondent, namely, the District Collector, South 24-Parganas.

3. The allegation in the writ petition is that the land on which the private respondents are putting up construction is a land which has been vested with the Government both under the provisions of the West Bengal Land Reforms Act and the West Bengal Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948.

entities.text: West Bengal Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Among the private respondents there are also legal heirs of the original raiyats who are supporting the stand taken by the writ petitioner by contending that the entire extent of land was acquired and compensation has been received.

4. Therefore, we direct the 3rd respondent, namely, the District Collector, South 24-Parganas to call for appropriate reports, records, documents from the respective officers under both the enactments where the vesting/acquisition is stated to have taken place.

Apart from that also reports, records,
documents to be called for from the 4 th respondent, namely, the Block Land and Land Reforms Officer, Kolkata Block with regard to the orders of conversion which may have been passed.

After examining all the records, a comprehensive report shall be submitted by the District Collector,
South 24-Parganas for consideration of this court.

5. List this matter on 19th December, 2024.
(T. S. SIVAGNANAM) CHIEF JUSTICE (HIRANMAY BHATTACHARYYA, J.)
